blocks.text:
The day's programme depends on water levels, the weather and wildlife activity. Early morning is the best time for sightings. At dawn, caimans, capybaras, anteaters and many birds come out near the water and along the roads.

The Pantanal changes with the water level. Some roads stay dry while others pass flooded stretches, so safaris rarely follow the same pattern. The guides follow the animals' movements, which gives you a better chance of seeing them in their natural surroundings.

Your guides help you spot tracks in the damp ground, movement in the tall grass, and the nests of toucans and macaws. Along the way you may see large termite mounds, giant water lilies and trees occupied by colonies of storks and ibises.

Some routes take you on horseback across flooded savanna and small patches of woodland. The open terrain gives you time to watch the animals, and the guides adapt each outing to where wildlife is most active that day.

blocks.text:
Set off early for Bonito, a region of clear rivers, limestone caves and tropical forest. On the way, you'll visit Estancia Mimosa ranch.

The route follows the Mimoso River through the forest, past hills and waterfalls. Boardwalks and dirt paths lead across small bridges and past viewpoints and swimming spots. Water cascades over the limestone into clear natural pools.

The visit includes a stop at the observatory, a short boat ride and a water attraction with a 6-metre platform. After the walk, lunch featuring local produce is served in the main building. You can then rest in the hammocks before transferring to Bonito and checking in at Arte da Natureza.
